findings.title: Ticker change runs every cleanup job ten times more often
findings.body: Changing the global cleanup ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute affects all jobs in clean(), not only annotation cleanup: expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, user invites, short URLs, and query history will also run ten times as often. This increases database and filesystem load and lock contention on every Grafana instance, is unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix described in the PR, and is not documented or made configurable. The interval should be reverted to 10 minutes or separately justified and scoped to annotations only.

findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors with full ID lists
findings.body: The new cleanup paths at lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579 call r.log.Error unconditionally after successful fetches/deletes, passing a nil err and the entire ids slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 IDs in the new test). Normal cleanup will therefore emit multiple huge error-level log lines per batch per annotation type, flooding logs, triggering error alerting, and masking real failures. These should be Debug-level (or removed), should not log the full ID list, and errors should only be logged where they are actually returned.

findings.title: deleteByIDs can exceed parameter limits on non-SQLite databases
findings.body: For every database except the special-cased SQLite path, deleteByIDs builds a single DELETE with one placeholder per fetched ID, and the number of IDs is bounded only by the configurable AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize. PostgreSQL and MySQL prepared statements are limited to 65535 parameters, so a larger configured batch size that previously worked with the subquery DELETE will now fail on every batch and abort cleanup. The delete should be chunked into bounded groups for all dialects rather than only working around SQLite.

findings.title: SQLite ID list construction is quadratic for large batches
findings.body: The SQLite branch rebuilds the IN list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) inside the loop, copying the entire accumulated string on every iteration. For the 32767-ID batch exercised by the new test this is O(n^2) copying (gigabytes of intermediate copying) on each affected annotation type, undermining the large-batch support the branch is meant to add. Build the list with strings.Builder or strings.Join instead.
